- Model consistently overestimates prices in the early part of the 30-day horizon, especially after recent spikes; reduce initial forecast values by 1–3% for high-sentiment periods.
- After a price spike (e.g., >80), model tends to overshoot and then decay too slowly; apply a “cool-down” correction: subtract 0.5–1.5% per day after peak.
- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.67) and price is rising, model overreacts; dampen forecast slope by 10–20% for 3–5 days.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤0.33) mid-horizon, model fails to adjust downward; apply a downward bias of 0.5–1.0% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
- Mean reversion is strong in the final 5–7 days; model often underestimates downward correction; add 0.2–0.8% per day to forecast for the last 7 days if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- For events with official announcements (e.g., policy changes, auction results), model often lags by 1–2 days; adjust forecast 1–2 days ahead of event if sentiment is positive.
- If true outcome shows a sharp drop after a peak, model fails to recognize it; add a “drop buffer” of 0.5–1.0% per day for 3–5 days after peak if sentiment is mixed or negative.
